item.title: Headline Above the Coach

turns.text: Make a 4:5 social image of a smiling female fitness coach in a bright studio. Put “Start where you are” at the top, not over her face. Keep it upbeat, no other text.

item.tests: Checks that the finished composition reserves top space for the headline and keeps the face unobscured.

answer_sheet.Headline and other wording: Use exactly “Start where you are” and no other text.
answer_sheet.Headline placement: At the top of the image, above the coach's face, without overlapping it.
answer_sheet.Size or platform: 4:5 portrait social image; no particular platform.
answer_sheet.Person and setting: An invented smiling female fitness coach in a bright studio; no reference photo.

must_haves: The headline reads exactly “Start where you are” and sits in the top portion of the image.
No headline letters overlap the coach's face; her full face remains visible.
A smiling female fitness coach is clearly depicted in a bright studio.
The headline is readable, fully inside the canvas, and accompanied by no other text.

approvals.name: generate_image

args.name: Start Where You Are — Fitness Coach

style.prompt: Create an upbeat polished photorealistic social media image featuring a smiling adult female fitness coach in a bright airy fitness studio with soft daylight, pale walls, subtle fitness equipment, vibrant teal athletic clothing, friendly approachable expression, natural realistic anatomy. Medium waist-up portrait, face located clearly below the headline area. Design for ultimate mobile glance legibility. At the top place the exact words "Start where you are" in very large bold clean dark navy sans-serif lettering, preferably two lines: "Start where" then "you are". Headline has strong contrast on a clean light warm cream background, generous padding, no busy details behind it. All lettering completely above her head and face with a generous visible gap; never overlap her face or hair. No other text, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, signage or branding. Encouraging, positive and welcoming rather than intimidating. Keep all important content in the central portion with generous extra background at top and bottom so it can be recomposed to a 4:5 portrait image.
